about.title: About — Tim Chen
about.description: Tim Chen is a C#/.NET backend engineer. Gogoro, Titansoft, language study in Tokyo, and JLPT N1.
about.heading: About
about.lead: Yu-Ting Chen. I work on C# and .NET backends that are already running: pull the slow ones back, remove calls that should not be there, and split logic nobody wants to touch until it can be tested.
about.engineering: Since March 2026 I have been a .NET backend engineer at Gogoro, on the performance and reliability of existing services. From August 2020 to April 2023 I was a Product Developer at Titansoft, building REST and gRPC microservices, including an internship there in 2020.
about.projects: Among the public programs, Discipline App is a Pomodoro timer connected to Google Calendar, and TwStock is a Taiwan stock-data service split into Api, Application, Domain, and Infrastructure. TimeMiner and Level are earlier.
about.japan: I can work in Japanese. From April 2024 to October 2025 I studied at Eastwest Japanese Language School in Tokyo. JLPT N1.
about.sharing: At Titansoft I ran an engineering reading group. The topics were problems that were actually stuck at the time.
about.life: Outside work I ride and hike.

tools.title: Developer tools
tools.lead: Timestamp, JSON, YAML, MD5, encoding, JWT, plus URL, UUID, regex, base conversion, text diff, and identifier case. After the page loads, the calculations run in this browser.
tools.privacy: Inputs are processed in this browser and are not sent away for calculation

timestamp.pasteHint: Paste a number to convert. Up to 10 digits is seconds; around 13 digits is milliseconds.
timestamp.dateHint: Without a timezone, this is your computer's local time.
timestamp.offsetHint: Anchored to now. Choose an amount and a unit, and the date and timestamp appear below.

json.shortcut: Pasting JSON formats it immediately. Ctrl or ⌘ + Enter works too.

yaml.placeholder: Paste YAML. You can also paste JSON and convert it

md5.drop: Drop a file here, or click to choose
md5.dropHint: Hashed in this browser. Nothing is uploaded

jwt.placeholder: Paste a JWT. A leading Bearer prefix is removed
jwt.secretPlaceholder: Only needed to verify HS256 / HS384 / HS512
jwt.sampleHint: Both samples use the secret: secret
jwt.algNote: Decoding needs no secret, and the token stays on this device. Verification supports HMAC only.

errors.invalid-number: That is not a timestamp. Put dates in the field on the right.
errors.invalid-date: Could not read that date. Try 2024-01-02 15:04:05
errors.invalid-relative: Enter a whole number from 0 up, and choose a unit.
errors.invalid-utf8: Those bytes are not valid UTF-8 text
errors.invalid-jwt: That does not look like a JWT. It needs header.payload.signature
errors.out-of-range: That time is outside the supported range
errors.unsupported-alg: Only HS256, HS384, and HS512 can be verified
errors.yaml-missing: The YAML parser did not load
errors.too-large: More than 400 lines. Shorten the text before comparing.

url.placeholder: Paste text, a URL, or a=1&b=2

uuid.hint: Uses this browser’s random numbers. Nothing is sent away.

radix.placeholder: Paste a number, such as 255 or 0xff

tools.pageDescription: Timestamp, JSON, YAML, hashes, encoding, JWT, URL, UUID, regex, base conversion, text diff, and identifier case in the browser. Inputs are not sent away for processing.

diff.hint: Compared line by line. Newlines are normalized first, and a final newline does not count as a difference.

case.hint: A run of capitals stays one word, so HTTPResponse splits into http and response.

home.title: Tim Chen — Backend Software Engineer
home.description: Tim Chen (Yu-Ting Chen). I make C#/.NET systems that are already running faster, quieter, and safe to change. Currently at Gogoro.
home.lead: Yu-Ting Chen. I work on systems that are already running: pull slow APIs back, remove calls that should not be there, and split logic nobody wants to change until it can be tested. Currently at Gogoro.
home.resultsNote: Three changes on systems that were already running. Each one has the problem, what I changed, and the result.
home.result1Body: When a checksum did not match, the same fallback API ran again. That path was about 75,000 calls a day, and most of them were unnecessary. After the fix it is under 50 a day, about 99.9% fewer.
home.result2Title: APIs people had to wait on
home.result2Body: A few APIs that took over 2 seconds now respond in about 200 milliseconds. Set 2 seconds against 200 milliseconds, and that is about ten times faster.
home.result3Title: Calculation that could not be tested alone
home.result3Body: After maintenance-notice calculation, the service, and the clock were split apart, station aggregation, range merging, and the cache can each be checked. Tests that had been failing were fixed too.
home.gogoroBody: Performance and reliability of existing .NET services: which calls are unnecessary, which APIs are actually slow, and which logic people are afraid to change.
home.titansoftBody: Product backends: REST and gRPC microservices, SQL Server, Redis, and Kafka. With the team I helped bring integration testing into everyday development, and I ran an engineering reading group. Includes a 2020 internship.
home.schoolBody: B.S. in Computer Science. Third place, Information Applications, 2019 International ICT Innovative Services Awards (a university project with classmates).
home.contactLead: If you want another case, or just to compare backgrounds, email is enough.

work.description: Tim Chen's cases: extra fallback calls, API response time, and calculation that can be checked once it is split apart.
work.title: Cases
work.lead: Each one is a change to a system that was already running: the problem, what I changed, and what the numbers became.
work.case1Title: A checksum mismatch caused about 75,000 unnecessary fallback calls a day
work.case1Problem: When the checksum did not match, the system called a fallback API again. Those calls were about 75,000 a day, and most of them were unnecessary.
work.case1Action: I found and fixed the checksum mismatch so the fallback is sent only when it is actually needed.
work.case1Result: Daily calls to that fallback API fell from about 75,000 to under 50, about 99.9% fewer.
work.case2Title: APIs that took over 2 seconds, brought to about 200 milliseconds
work.case2Problem: Some APIs took more than 2 seconds to respond. People using them had to stop and wait.
work.case2Action: I changed only the APIs that measurements showed were actually over 2 seconds.
work.case2Result: Those APIs now respond in about 200 milliseconds. Set more than 2 seconds against about 200 milliseconds, and that is about ten times faster.
work.case3Title: Maintenance-notice calculation could be changed once it was split apart
work.case3Problem: Calculation and the service were written together, and the clock was hard to replace, so station data, merged time ranges, and the cache were hard to test on their own. Changing that logic meant checking it by hand.
work.case3Action: I split calculation from the service, injected the clock, and added tests for aggregation, range merging, and caching.
work.case3Result: Range merging and the cache can be tested on their own, and the tests that had been failing were fixed. Over the same period the unit tests in this area grew from 41 to more than 400, covering aggregation, range merging, and the cache. The larger suite is a result of that split, not the goal.
work.treeNote: Links to these projects are on Projects.
work.disciplineBody: A Pomodoro timer and daily tasks that can be opened every day. Finished work adds experience points, and the app connects to Google Calendar and Google Tasks. Sign-in is Google OAuth. It runs on Azure App Service and is published with GitHub Actions. ASP.NET Core Blazor Server, .NET 7, Entity Framework Core, and SQLite.
work.twstockBody: Taiwan stock data comes in from the TWSE and FinMind, lands in SQL Server, and is read back through the API. The service is split into Api, Application, Domain, and Infrastructure, and the domain has unit tests. The frontend is Next.js.
work.timeminerBody: A work-time log. It stores custom tables and records work time. ASP.NET Core MVC and Entity Framework Core, on Azure.
work.levelBody: A practice log built with Flutter and Firebase. It was on Google Play.
